## The change

Uncommitted on branch `fix/bad-080-hot-seat` in this worktree. `git diff` and `git status` show it: `main.js`, `renderer/app.js`, `preload.js`, `web/collabweb-sync.js`, `web/booth.js`, `web/CLAUDE.md`, `renderer/CLAUDE.md`, and a new `test/collabdelivery.test.js`.

The ticket: a collab room in `wrapping` becomes `wrapped` **on read**, and both clients opened a take's push with an `info` call — so the pusher itself completed the wrap under its own delivery, spending BAD-063's `WRAP_GRACE_MS` on the ordinary path instead of on the race it was written for. Ratte's fix takes the read off the delivery path in both clients and holds the booth's *idle* heartbeat while a take is owed.

## The claims to verify — these are the job

Each of these is load-bearing. For each, say CONFIRMED or NOT, with the file and line you read it in. Do not accept the comment's word for it; the comments are the thing under test.

1. **`completeWrap` probes the seat BEFORE the handler restamps/nulls `recording_at`.** This single ordering claim is what makes three separate decisions safe: the hot idle beat going out unheld, `booth.js`'s stop beat staying where it is (ahead of the decode and save), and `renderer/app.js`'s `stopRecording` beat likewise. If the probe actually happens *after* the write, a stop beat can complete a wrap and the fix has a hole exactly where it claims not to. Read `server/supabase/functions/collab/room.ts` and `_shared/collab.mjs`; trace the heartbeat handler end to end.
2. **`upload-url` and `commit` are the only modes `loadRoom` stands aside for**, and every other mode — `info`, `heartbeat`, `pull`, `status`, whatever else exists — completes a wrapping room's wrap. Enumerate the modes; confirm nothing else on a client's normal path is also a read that wraps and has been missed. In particular: does anything in the delivery sequence *other* than upload-url/commit hit the room? The storage PUT goes to the bucket, not the function — confirm that.
3. **The snapshot the push now decides against is always fresh enough to be correct.** Web reads `collab.info`; main reads `collabInfoSnaps`. Verify that `pendingPushes` given a stale snapshot cannot *lose* a take (send nothing when something was owed) rather than merely delay it, and cannot *double-send* one. Ratte documented one known cost — a seat claimed in the last instant may miss the first push, recovered by the trailing refresh and the 60s poll. Confirm that is the only such case, and that the recovery path he names actually exists and runs.
4. **The idle-beat hold cannot lapse a seat.** `collabTakeInFlight()` reads `collabPushInFlight || collabSync.debounce || collabSync.queued.push`. Check that every one of those clears on *every* exit path, error and early-return included — a flag stuck true holds the heartbeat forever and the seat lapses at `CLAIM_LEASE_MS`. The web sets its flag inside `pushTakes` under `try/finally`; the renderer sets it in `runCollabSync` around the IPC with `.finally()`; main uses a `collabDelivering` Set under `try/finally`. Look for a path that returns before the flag is set but after the debounce cleared, and say whether the gap matters.
5. **The two clients actually agree.** This is one rule in two places. Name any behavioural difference between the web and desktop halves and say whether it is a real divergence or a necessary consequence of the process split (main computes `pending`, so the renderer cannot know before it calls).
6. **The TDZ question.** `collab:push` at `main.js:~4040` reads `collabInfoSnaps` and `collabDelivering`, both `const`-declared later in `registerIpc()` at ~4381. Confirm they are in the same function scope and that no path can invoke the handler before `registerIpc()` finishes executing.
7. **The new test is a real pin, not a tautology.** `test/collabdelivery.test.js` drives `web/collabweb-sync.js` in a vm and greps structure for the Electron halves. Ratte reports that restoring HEAD's `collabweb-sync.js` failed 7 of its 11 tests. Check what the other 4 pin and whether the regex-based assertions on `main.js` / `renderer/app.js` would survive a rename or a reformat that keeps the bug — a pin that passes on broken code is worse than no pin. Say which assertions are brittle and which are load-bearing.
